title: Italian Turkey Meatball Subs
subtitle: tender baked turkey meatballs simmered in marinara, piled into toasted rolls under melted provolone
imageAlt: Two meatball subs with tomato sauce and melted provolone in toasted rolls on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 4 subs: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Wet your hands to roll the meatballs; the mix is soft and that keeps them tender.
Thaw frozen ground turkey in the fridge overnight.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Mix the turkey, panko, egg, Parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper gently with your hands.

steps.title: Roll and bake
steps.text: Roll into 16 meatballs with wet hands and set them on the sheet. Bake 15–18 minutes, until browned and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Warm the marinara in a large skillet, add the meatballs and simmer 5 minutes, turning to coat.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Turn the oven to broil. Split the rolls without cutting through, open them on the sheet and toast 1–2 minutes, watching closely.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Fill each roll with 4 meatballs and sauce, tear a slice of provolone over the top and broil 1–2 minutes until melted.

fixIt.fix: Turkey is lean; mix gently and pull them at 74°C (165°F) exactly.
Chill the rolled meatballs 10 minutes before baking.
Toast them first and spoon on less sauce; serve extra for dipping.

saleTip: Ground turkey is often $4.99 for 450 g on sale at No Frills; hoagie rolls are in the bakery aisle.
swap: Lean ground beef: bake to 71°C (160°F). Mozzarella for provolone.
leftovers: Keep meatballs in sauce and build fresh subs.
doneness: Ground turkey to 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada, ground poultry).
source: Based on tested baked turkey meatball methods (Canadian Living, Budget Bytes): panko-and-Parmesan turkey meatballs baked at 200°C, simmered in marinara and broiled in rolls with provolone.
prepAhead: Roll the meatballs up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge.
Bake and freeze meatballs up to 3 months; reheat in the sauce from frozen, 15 minutes.
reheat: Meatballs in sauce covered over medium 8–10 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Turkey meatballs in marinara on toasted rolls; no Parmesan or Italian seasoning in the mix.

stepNotes.0: Basic: skip the Parmesan and Italian seasoning.

fancy.note: Garlic-butter toasted rolls and a little extra Parmesan on top.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: spread the rolls with the butter mashed with the garlic powder before toasting.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: scatter the Parmesan over the provolone before broiling.

plating: Wrap each sub halfway in parchment.
Extra warm sauce in a small dish.
A pickle spear on the side.

why.0-1: Panko soaks up juices so lean turkey stays moist.
why.0-3: Parmesan adds the savoury depth turkey lacks on its own.
why.1-2: Provolone melts smoothly and has a mild tang.

funFact: Canadians call it a sub, hoagie or grinder depending on where they grew up; 'sub' comes from the submarine shape.

keeps.note: freeze meatballs in sauce, not built subs
